toml:
# Ground-contact planning: three illustrative satellites over three illustrative stations for
# 12 hours. The run gives each satellite-station pass its access window and the data volume
# DVB-S2 adaptive coding and modulation (ACM) can move in it (ETSI EN 302 307-1 Table 13
# thresholds plus an implementation margin). It then builds a conflict-free contact plan in
# which each antenna serves one satellite at a time, with a turnaround between contacts, and
# each satellite downlinks to one station at a time. Delivery is weighted by priority and
# capped at each satellite's backlog. Three plans are reported side by side: a marginal-value
# greedy, a first-come baseline and, when the candidate set is small, the exact optimum, with
# the greedy's optimality gap.
#
# Every number below is ILLUSTRATIVE: no operator's orbits, stations or link budget.
# MODELLED: the scheduler is checked against its own exact solver, not an external tool.
kind = "contact-schedule"
epoch = [2024.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
duration_hours = 12.0
step_s = 30.0
refraction = true
light_time = true

[link]
frequency_ghz = 8.2            # X-band downlink
eirp_dbw = 7.0
symbol_rate_msps = 20.0
other_losses_db = 2.0
zenith_atm_loss_db = 0.3
implementation_margin_db = 1.0
acm_step_s = 10.0

[[satellites]]
name = "eo-sso-a"
altitude_km = 550.0
inclination_deg = 97.6
raan_deg = 0.0
arg_lat_deg = 0.0
backlog_mbit = 400000.0
priority = 2.0

[[satellites]]
name = "eo-sso-b"
altitude_km = 550.0
inclination_deg = 97.6
raan_deg = 0.0
arg_lat_deg = 180.0
backlog_mbit = 400000.0
priority = 1.0

[[satellites]]
name = "iot-mid"
altitude_km = 700.0
inclination_deg = 53.0
raan_deg = 60.0
arg_lat_deg = 90.0
backlog_mbit = 60000.0
priority = 1.5

[[stations]]
name = "polar-north"
lat_deg = 78.2
lon_deg = 15.4
alt_m = 450.0
mask_deg = 5.0
g_over_t_db = 30.0
setup_s = 120.0

[[stations]]

lat_deg = 52.2
lon_deg = 5.0
alt_m = 10.0
mask_deg = 5.0

[[stations]]

setup_s = 120.0
